title: Pandu and Dhritarashtra
body:
Pandu and Dhritarashtra

Because Dhritarashtra was born blind, he was disqualified from inheriting the crown according to the Kuru royal laws. Thus, Pandu, the younger brother, ascended the throne of Hastinapur. Dhritarashtra remained in the palace, doting on his silent contemplation and harbouring a deep, internal attachment to the physical realm.
Pandu was a capable and victorious king who expanded the borders of Hastinapur. He married Kunti and Madri. However, his glorious reign was cut short by a tragic error. While hunting in the forest, Pandu shot a pair of deer mating, unaware that they were Sage Kindama and his wife in disguise. The dying sage pronounced a terrifying curse: 'If you ever seek intimacy with your wives, you shall die at that very instant.'
Stricken with remorse and unable to rule, Pandu abdicated his throne, retired to the forest with his two wives, and spent his days in rigorous penance. In his absence, Dhritarashtra was appointed the caretaker sovereign, ruling Hastinapur under the watchful, protective guidance of Bheeshma and Vidura. During their stay in the forest, Pandu lamented his childlessness, prompting Kunti to reveal her divine mantra.
